newsitem.title: FRANCE: L'Oreal no comment on Nestle changes.
newsitem.headline: L'Oreal no comment on Nestle changes.

text.p: L'Oreal chairman Lindsay Owen-Jones said on Wednesday he was not aware of any change in the way Nestle regarded its stake in L'Oreal resulting from changes in senior management at the Swiss food company.

"I can't say what's going on at Nestle," Owen-Jones told a news conference. He said Nestle had consistently described its stake in L'Oreal as a strategic investment and he had seen no indication of any change.

Nestle owns 49 percent of Gesparal, the company that controls L'Oreal. The other 51 percent is owned by the Bettencourt family. A 20-year standstill agreement between the Gesparal partners ended in 1994.
Nestle will have a new chief executive in June when Peter Brabeck replaces Helmut Maucher, who will however remain in his post as chairman.
